plan.title: Overdeck MCP server: pan mcp serve, /mcp endpoint and Copy MCP URL
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: Parent PRD: Overdeck Anywhere revision 5 (W-INT2, FR-27, D-21)

narratives.Problem: Outside tools (another agent harness, a chat bot) cannot drive Overdeck: there is no MCP control surface, only the per-agent Channels bridge. Answering prompts has no scope narrower than admin.
narratives.Proposal: One MCP tool module under src/lib/mcp/ that proxies the dashboard's existing REST routes with the caller's Bearer odk_ token, served over stdio by `pan mcp serve` and over stateless streamable HTTP at POST /mcp. A new approve scope guards the eight approval routes; three route-scope rows open search and the two spawn routes to MCP tokens; a new POST /api/workers route wraps startWorker(). Settings → Anywhere gains Copy MCP URL (mints a non-admin token, copies <address>/mcp and shows the header and client config) and an Access tokens panel with revoke. Docs: configuration/mcp.mdx plus the scope tables.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Fleet reach: MCP reaching linked machines' conversations (PAN-4651).
- Any change to the Channels bridge (src/lib/channels/overdeck-bridge.ts).
- Stateful MCP sessions, SSE streams, server-initiated notifications, MCP resources or prompts.
- OAuth for MCP clients; the only credential is a Bearer odk_ token.
- A token in the URL (query string or path).
- MCP tools for pane-choice menus, pi asks, Codex approvals, plan approvals or agent questions (their routes still get the approve row).
- Serving /mcp through the Vite dev server (pan dev).
- A `pan mcp token` convenience verb.
- Accepting root credentials, paired-device credentials or admin-scoped tokens on /mcp or pan mcp serve.
- Changing what admin, operate or tell allow beyond the three new FR-3 rows.

autoDecisions.summary: The token travels in the Authorization header; Copy MCP URL copies <address>/mcp and offers the header and a client config.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-2351 D-10 forbids tokens in URLs and resolveDashboardCredential reads kind token credentials only from the Bearer header; 'with the token' in the parent PRD is met by the config block (D-4649-1).

autoDecisions.summary: /mcp runs the streamable HTTP transport in stateless JSON mode with GET/DELETE answering 405.
autoDecisions.rationale: No session bookkeeping, revocation is 'next request fails', and the tools need no server-initiated messages (D-4649-2).

autoDecisions.summary: Default MCP token scopes are read:state, read:conversations, operate; approve only via an unchecked-by-default checkbox; admin never.
autoDecisions.rationale: operate covers tell and the two spawn routes; D-21 says approve is off by default and MCP is always fenced (D-4649-3).

autoDecisions.summary: Both transports proxy the existing dashboard routes with the caller's Bearer token; the tool module never calls src/lib operation functions.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the route-scope table the only scope authority, making D-21's 'no second path' true by construction.

autoDecisions.summary: /mcp does its own credential check and refuses root credentials, device credentials and admin-scoped tokens.
autoDecisions.rationale: /mcp is outside the remote gate's prefixes; accepting admin would let MCP change settings, which D-21 forbids (D-4649-4).

autoDecisions.summary: answer_question enforces approve in the tool layer and serves Claude Code conversations only.
autoDecisions.rationale: The dashboard answers a Claude Code AskUserQuestion via the tell-scoped message route; the tool must add the approve check itself, and the docs state that send_message can still deliver text (D-4649-5, D-4649-6).

autoDecisions.summary: pan mcp serve takes its token only from OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN and verifies it locally at start.
autoDecisions.rationale: An argv token shows in ps; an internal-token fallback would be admin and violate 'always fenced' (D-4649-7).

autoDecisions.summary: search_conversations uses GET /api/palette/search with a new read:conversations row and returns only the conversations array.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is the existing conversation search route; its other arrays are derived from conversations (D-4649-8).

autoDecisions.summary: Starting a worker gets a new POST /api/workers route that calls startWorker() in-process.
autoDecisions.rationale: No worker-start route exists; startWorker is the same core pan worker run uses, and the server already calls spawnRun in-process (D-4649-11).

autoDecisions.summary: Low-level SDK Server with hand-written JSON Schemas; no zod.
autoDecisions.rationale: zod is not a direct dependency and overdeck-bridge.ts already uses this pattern (D-4649-12).

autoDecisions.summary: machine accepts omitted, auto, this machine's label or id; everything else is a tool error.
autoDecisions.rationale: Fleet reach is PAN-4651's; this machine's half needs no links (D-4649-13).

autoDecisions.summary: Revocation from Settings → Anywhere is a general Access tokens panel over the existing GET/DELETE /api/access-tokens routes.
autoDecisions.rationale: The parent threat model requires revoking MCP tokens from Settings → Anywhere and today that page lists only paired devices; a general panel needs no new record field.

metadata.sizeJustification: This issue is already the per-machine slice of one epic work item (W-INT2). Its done criterion — an MCP client configured from Copy MCP URL lists and messages conversations and gets 403 on a settings change — needs the scope, the routes, both transports, the Settings UI and the docs together. The file count is inflated by one test file per source file, and the subsystem count by each docs page (configuration/*, docs/*, cli/*, docs.json, package.json) counting as its own subsystem. The work is still decomposed into 14 small items with real-dependency edges only.

items.title: Add the approve access-token scope

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-1. In src/lib/access-tokens.ts line 42 insert 'approve' between 'operate' and 'admin' in ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPES; scopeSatisfies stays unchanged so only admin implies approve. Update the module header comment to list approve as an independent grant. In src/cli/commands/token.ts line 111 the --scopes help text becomes 'Comma-separated scopes: read:events, read:state, read:conversations, tell, operate, approve, admin'. Add the four W-1 assertions to tests/unit/lib/access-tokens.test.ts.

items.title: Given a token with scopes ['operate'], when scopeSatisfies(scopes, 'approve') runs, then it returns false; with ['admin'] or ['approve'] it returns true.
Given the input 'read:state,approve', when parseAccessTokenScopes runs, then it returns ['read:state','approve'] instead of throwing an unknown-scope error.
Given `pan token create --help`, then the --scopes option text lists approve between operate and admin.

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-2. Append only; do not reorder existing rows (PAN-4645 also edits this table). Add requiredScopeFor assertions for all eight paths plus an unchanged admin case to src/dashboard/server/__tests__/route-scopes.test.ts.

items.title: Given each FR-2 route with sample segments (for example POST /api/conversations/conv-1/permission and POST /api/agents/agent-pan-1/permissions/req-1/respond), when requiredScopeFor runs, then it returns 'approve'.
Given POST /api/conversations/conv-1/archive, when requiredScopeFor runs, then it still returns 'admin'.

items.title: Given GET /api/palette/search, when requiredScopeFor runs, then it returns 'read:conversations'.
Given POST /api/conversations or POST /api/workers, when requiredScopeFor runs, then it returns 'operate'.

Create src/dashboard/server/routes/workers.ts exporting parseStartWorkerBody, startWorkerFromBody(body, start = startWorker) and workersRouteLayer. Auth via rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest. Tests in src/dashboard/server/__tests__/workers-route.test.ts with an injected start function. No execSync.

items.title: Given a body missing issueId, an empty prompt, harness 'vim' or effort 'huge', when parseStartWorkerBody runs, then it returns ok:false with an error naming that field.

Given a valid body and a fake start that resolves { id: 'agent-pan-1-worker-1', cwd: '/w', branch: 'b' }, when startWorkerFromBody runs, then it returns status 200 with that object and the fake received parentId null.
Given a fake start that throws Error('PAN-1 has no workspace at /x'), when startWorkerFromBody runs, then it returns status 400 with error 'PAN-1 has no workspace at /x'.
Given the no-loss matrix, then it contains a row whose surface is 'POST /api/workers'.
Create the MCP tool module core with the four read tools

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Creates only new files under src/lib/mcp/ and tests/unit/lib/mcp/; no other item touches them until its DAG successors run.

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-5. ALL_TOOLS = [...READ_TOOLS] in this item. The module imports only Node built-ins, the SDK, ../access-tokens.js and ../config.js; never dashboard server code; never calls src/lib operation functions (every tool proxies a route). Tests in tests/unit/lib/mcp/tools-read.test.ts via SDK Client + InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair and a recording fake DashboardApi. Honor the list_conversations key-name implementation checkpoint and its fallback.

items.title: Given an SDK client connected through InMemoryTransport, when it calls tools/list, then the names are exactly list_machines, list_conversations, search_conversations, read_conversation.
Given a fake API, when list_conversations runs with no arguments, then it calls GET /api/conversations?limit=50 and returns rows that carry only the projected keys.

Given a fake API that answers 403 { error: 'insufficient_scope', missingScope: 'read:conversations' }, when a read tool runs, then the result has isError true and its text contains missingScope read:conversations.

Given this machine's descriptor, when resolveMachine runs with undefined, 'auto', the label or the environmentId, then it returns ok:true; with 'laptop' it returns ok:false with the 'Unknown machine' error text.
Add send_message, start_conversation and start_worker tools

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-6. Create src/lib/mcp/tools-write.ts exporting WRITE_TOOLS: send_message (POST /api/conversations/<encoded name>/message { message }), start_conversation (resolveMachine first, then POST /api/conversations with only the given keys among message, projectKey, model, harness, effort, issueId; never cwd), start_worker (resolveMachine first, then POST /api/workers with issueId, prompt and the given optional keys). Set ALL_TOOLS = [...READ_TOOLS, ...WRITE_TOOLS] in src/lib/mcp/server.ts. Tests in tests/unit/lib/mcp/tools-write.test.ts.

items.title: Given send_message with conversation 'conv a' and message 'hi', when it runs, then the fake API receives POST /api/conversations/conv%20a/message with body { message: 'hi' }.
Given start_conversation with machine 'laptop', when it runs, then the result has isError true and the fake API records no POST.
Given start_conversation called with an extra cwd argument, when it runs, then the POST /api/conversations body has no cwd key.
Given start_worker with issueId and prompt, when it runs, then the fake API receives POST /api/workers with those fields.
Add list_pending_input, answer_question and answer_permission tools

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-7 and decisions D-4649-5/D-4649-6. Create src/lib/mcp/tools-approve.ts exporting APPROVE_TOOLS. answer_question checks scopeSatisfies(ctx.scopes, 'approve') before any request, then GET /api/conversations/<name>, refuses a harness other than claude-code/null/absent, then posts the composed 'Operator answered the pending question' message exactly as the PRD snippet. answer_permission validates choice in allow-once/allow-always/deny before posting { signature, choice } to POST /api/conversations/<name>/permission. Set ALL_TOOLS = [...READ_TOOLS, ...WRITE_TOOLS, ...APPROVE_TOOLS]. Tests in tests/unit/lib/mcp/tools-approve.test.ts.

items.title: Given scopes ['read:conversations','operate'], when answer_question runs, then the result has isError true naming the approve scope and the fake API records zero calls.

Given scopes including approve and a conversation whose harness is claude-code, when answer_question runs with answers ['yes'] and questions ['Ship it?'], then the fake API receives a message body starting 'Operator answered the pending question:' and containing 'Q: Ship it?\nA: yes'.
Given scopes including approve and a conversation whose harness is codex, when answer_question runs, then it returns the Claude-Code-only error and posts nothing.
Given answer_permission with choice 'maybe', when it runs, then it returns isError true and posts nothing; with 'allow-once' it posts { signature, choice } to the permission route.
Serve the tool module at POST /mcp in stateless JSON mode

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Its only shared files (server.ts, no-loss-matrix.ts) are serialized by the workers-route edge; routes/mcp.ts and its test are new.

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-8 and decision D-4649-4. Create src/dashboard/server/routes/mcp.ts exporting McpRouteDeps, makeMcpRouteLayer(deps) and mcpRouteLayer (makeApi uses createFetchDashboardApi with getDashboardLoopbackApiUrl(), never getDashboardApiUrl()). POST /mcp runs: validateOriginHeaders, internal token configured, resolveDashboardCredential (null 401), kind !== 'token' 403, admin scope 403; then a fresh WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined, enableJsonResponse: true }) and createOverdeckMcpServer({ api, scopes }). GET and DELETE /mcp answer 405 with Allow: POST. Cache-Control no-store everywhere. Register mcpRouteLayer in makeRoutesLayer before staticRouteLayer (server.ts line 355). Add no-loss-matrix rows for POST, GET and DELETE /mcp. Honor the toWeb/fromWeb implementation checkpoint and its fallback. Tests in src/dashboard/server/__tests__/mcp-route.test.ts following scoped-token-acceptance.test.ts.

items.title: Given POST /mcp with no credential, the internal token, an admin-scoped token, or a valid token plus Origin https://evil.example, when the route answers, then the statuses are 401, 403, 403 and 403 respectively.
Given GET /mcp, when the route answers, then it returns 405 with header Allow: POST and never the SPA index.html.

Given a token with read:conversations and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, when it posts a tools/list JSON-RPC request, then the route returns 200 JSON whose result.tools names equal ALL_TOOLS names.
Given that token is revoked with revokeAccessToken, when the same request is sent again, then the route returns 401.
Add pan mcp serve over stdio

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-9 and decision D-4649-7. Create src/cli/commands/mcp.ts exporting runMcpServe(deps) and registerMcpCommands(program) for `pan mcp serve`; static imports only Commander types and chalk, everything else loaded inside the handler. Token only from OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN; verify with refreshAccessTokens() + verifyAccessToken(); refuse missing, unknown/revoked, non-token-kind and admin tokens with exit 1 and the stderr texts in the PRD. Serve createOverdeckMcpServer({ api: createFetchDashboardApi({ baseUrl: getDashboardApiUrl(), token }), scopes }) over new StdioServerTransport(stdin, stdout). Nothing in this path writes to stdout except the transport. Add one import line and registerMcpCommands(program) after line 227 in src/cli/index.ts. Tests in tests/unit/cli/mcp.test.ts with a temporary OVERDECK_HOME and PassThrough streams.

items.title: Given OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN is unset, when runMcpServe runs, then it resolves 1 and stderr contains 'pan token create mcp --scopes read:state,read:conversations,operate'.
Given an admin-scoped token or a revoked token in OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN, when runMcpServe runs, then it resolves 1 and writes nothing to stdout.

Given a valid read:conversations token and PassThrough streams, when an initialize line and a tools/list line are written to stdin, then every stdout line parses as JSON-RPC and the tools/list result names equal ALL_TOOLS names.
Prove the done criterion end to end through /mcp and the real gate

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4649.md work item W-10. Create src/dashboard/server/__tests__/mcp-acceptance.test.ts. App = remoteRequestGateLayer + makeMcpRouteLayer + stub routes for GET /api/environment, GET /api/conversations, POST /api/conversations/:name/message, POST /api/conversations, GET /api/conversations/:id, POST /api/conversations/:id/permission and PUT /api/settings. makeApi(token) dispatches back into the same app with Authorization: Bearer <token> and peer 127.0.0.1 so every tool call passes the real gate and route-scope table. Mint tokens with createAccessToken using MCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES (and a second one adding approve). Cover the six PRD cases.

items.title: Given a token with MCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES, when an MCP client calls list_conversations then send_message through POST /mcp, then the result lists the stub's conversation names and the message stub records the sent text.
Given the same token, when PUT /api/settings is sent through the gate with it, then the response is 403 with error insufficient_scope and missingScope admin.
Given the same token, when tools/list runs, then no tool name contains settings, pair, token, device or vault.

Given the same token, when answer_permission runs, then the result has isError true with missingScope approve and the permission stub records no call; given a token that adds approve, then the stub records exactly one call.
Given the same token, when start_conversation runs, then the POST /api/conversations stub records one call.
